links.outcome: Change in LLM diagnosis when patient demographics varied in matched-pair vignettes
links.effect: Black patients OR 6.09 (95% CI 5.13-7.24) and Latine patients OR 9.57 (8.00-11.45) for MDD vs White; Asian patients OR 2.88 for AN; female patients OR 0.43 for AN vs males.
links.quote: Mixed-effects logistic regression with LLM as a random intercept revealed significant demographic biases: Black patients were over 6 times more likely to receive a major depressive disorder (MDD) diagnosis than White patients with identical presentations (odds ratio [OR] 6.09, 95% CI 5.13-7.24), Latine patients were over 9 times more likely (OR 9.57, 95% CI 8.00-11.45), and Asian patients were nearly 3 times more likely to receive an AN diagnosis (OR 2.88, 95% CI 2.44-3.42).

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic differences across demographic subgroups with identical clinical content
links.effect: Significant demographic biases in psychiatric diagnosis; Black OR 6.09 and Latine OR 9.57 for MDD, female OR 0.43 for AN; intermodel Fleiss kappa 0.410 for ambiguous vignettes.
links.quote: These findings demonstrate that LLMs exhibit systematic demographic biases in psychiatric diagnosis even when clinical content is held constant, revealing measurable patterns that can inform improvements to training data, model architecture, and clinical deployment frameworks.

screen.reason: Empirical vignette study evaluating algorithmic and demographic bias in LLM psychiatric diagnostic outputs across synthetic patient profiles. Does not evaluate a deployment practice or safeguard.
